title: DocumentGaps
description: Compatibility filename for existing-document inventory gaps. Absence never means that a test is clinically indicated. Organize v3 note: this file is a CHECKLIST-DRIVEN view of what a cancer-type checklist expected to see, and it is explicitly NOT the coverage filter. A source no checklist row anticipated — a novel report filed under 15_未分类资料/ — is still fully organized, inventoried and archived; it simply has no gap row here. Read readiness.json.projection_coverage for 「what did the archive hold and what of it reached a structured slot」; read this file only for 「what did the checklist expect and not find」. Treating this file as the completeness gate would silently erase every open-world source.

coverage_basis.description: OPTIONAL. When present, declares that completeness for this run was judged per SOURCE — every source has a raw original, a masked .md sidecar and a source_inventory row — and NOT by whether the cancer-type checklist rows were all satisfied. Only one value is legal because there is only one defensible basis: a checklist is a prompt for what to look for, never a filter deciding what counts as a document.

novel_sources_counted.description: OPTIONAL. true = kind=novel sources (filed under 15_) were included when judging coverage, which is the expected value under organize v3. false records an explicitly narrowed, auditable run. This flag exists because a checklist has no row for a document type nobody anticipated; recording that the open-world sources were counted keeps 「no gaps」 from quietly meaning 「nothing outside the checklist was looked at」.

reason_for_artifact.description: Why the existing document would help the requested organizational artifact; never a test recommendation.

disclaimer.const: Document inventory only; not a test or treatment recommendation.
